newsitem.title: UK: Telewest says concerned over BSkyB/BT link.
newsitem.headline: Telewest says concerned over BSkyB/BT link.

text.p: British cable operator Telewest Communications Plc expressed its concern on Wednesday over a venture in which BSkyB and British Telecom are joining forces.

BSkyB said earlier it was creating British Interactive Broadcasting (BIB) by teaming up with BT, Midland Bank and Japan's Matsushita to supply interactive services to TV viewers and subsidise set-top boxes.

"With respect to BIB, our only concern will be to ensure that a joint venture involving quasi monopolists does not lead to anti-competitive behaviour. We are sure regulatory bodies will share this concern," Telewest's chief executive Stephen Davidson said.
BSkyB plans to launch its 200 channel digital satellite television venture in spring 1998 with each set-top box expected to be sold at around 200 pounds.
He said its customers did not have to pay for its set-top box and it was already designed to give access to Sky television prgrammes and to digital terrestrial television when it is launched.
"Our customers can thus avoid both unnecessary capital outlay and the complications of needing both BT and Sky in order to do what we will do...," Davidson said.
Meanwhile, UK's telecoms watchdog Oftel said that it was not its job to approve the joint venture but would only watch closely how it operated after it was launched.
